notes:
This short typescript continues the bottom corollary of scan 2, beginning with “ment” to complete “élément”. It states that the stabilizer in W of a regular line normalized by a Coxeter element c is the cyclic group generated by c; for each prescribed primitive h-th eigenvalue there is a unique Coxeter element normalizing that line. It states transitivity on the “droites cycliques” and their number card(W)/h. The NB asserts a free action of (Z/hZ)* commuting with W, with its orbits characterized by equality of stabilizers in W.

The normalizer, uniqueness and counting deductions were checked conditionally on the eigenvalue bound, regular-vector stabilizer property, transitivity and primitive-power conjugacy used in the preceding page. The unit-group action can be constructed by choosing a primitive root ζ, taking the unique c_D that acts on D by ζ, and sending D to its ζ^n eigenspace under c_D. The order, composition, commutation, freeness and equal-stabilizer assertions follow under those inputs; the cited root-system inputs were not independently established. CHECK_EVENTS.tsv gives the precise scope.

The mathematics made the normalizer argument D/W a locus for close reading, but the image controls the decision: a D overtypes a visible W. The canceled de beneath the opening pr of primitive is retained, and the raised ordinal is kept at its actual position rather than moved to the position favored by mathematical prose. The literal “une unique élément” is retained. There is no explicit mathematical doubt or unverified step written on this sheet, and no title, date or document page count. The archival sheet number is 2 (comment only). H’s following unnumbered “Lissification” heading is explicitly assigned to an adjacent unselected sheet and was excluded from this page’s witness packet; it is not an H error on this page.

The initial c and the unit-group star are handwritten according to all three image readings; that medium is marked in the consolidated file and inventory. Their unchanged glyphs are not counted as witness reading differences merely because one macro set lacks a handwriting wrapper. The quotation marks are upright typewriter double marks, not H’s guillemets. The only remaining doubts concern the ordinal’s accent and its unmarked syntactic attachment.

check_events.who: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort not exposed; main run
check_events.outcome: Let N be the line stabilizer. Its scalar action on a regular line is faithful, using the carried trivial-stabilizer premise. Its finite image in C* is cyclic and contains c of order h. A generator of the scalar image is an eigenvalue of a lift in W and has order at most h by the carried bound, hence N has order h and N=<c>. For a prescribed primitive eigenvalue, the powers c^k yield exactly one generator with that value; the preceding Coxeter criterion identifies it as Coxeter.

check_events.outcome: Assuming the stated W-transitivity on cyclic regular lines and their stabilizer <c> of order h, orbit-stabilizer gives their number |W|/h. This verifies the count from its premises, not the transitivity theorem.

check_events.who: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort not exposed; main run
check_events.outcome: Conditional construction: fix a primitive h-th root zeta. For each line D let c_D be its unique Coxeter stabilizer element with eigenvalue zeta. For n a unit mod h define n.D to be the zeta^n eigenline of c_D; existence and one-dimensional regularity use the carried primitive-power conjugacy and eigenvector statements. Then c_(n.D)=c_D^(n^-1), so m.(n.D)=(mn).D. Equality n.D=D forces zeta^n=zeta, hence n=1. Conjugation sends c_D to c_(wD), proving commutation with W. Unit-related lines have the same cyclic stabilizer. Conversely, a regular line with the same stabilizer is an eigenline of c_D with a primitive eigenvalue, hence n.D for a unique unit n. Replacing zeta by zeta^a replaces c_D by c_D^a and yields the same action, because a is invertible modulo h.

check_events.outcome: For a in the acting unit group and w in W, commutation gives w(aD)=a(wD). Since a is invertible, w(aD)=aD if and only if wD=D. Thus Stab_W(aD)=Stab_W(D).; This verifies the same-orbit implies same-stabilizer direction directly from the commuting-action hypothesis printed here. Freeness is not needed for this implication.; The converse, existence of the action, and its freeness are asserted on the page and were not proved.

check_events.who: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort not exposed; p03_r2
check_events.outcome: For a finite transitive W-action on these lines, the map W to the orbit of D has fibers the cosets of Stab_W(D), so the number of lines is card(W)/card(Stab_W(D)). Substituting the displayed cyclic stabilizer and, conditionally, its order h gives card(W)/h.; The written denominator h is consistent with a cyclic stabilizer of order h.; This is an elementary conditional count. I did not establish the order of a Coxeter element from this page, nor prove the claimed transitivity or the primitive-eigenvalue uniqueness assertion.

If the asserted generator c has order h, N_W(D)=<c> gives |W|/h, matching card(W)/h.; This checks the algebraic implication only. The order of c, finiteness, transitivity, and the normalizer theorem were not proved from this isolated page or checked externally.

check_events.outcome: For g in the acting group and D a line, w(gD)=g(wD). If wD=D then w(gD)=gD. Applying g inverse gives the reverse containment of stabilizers. Thus Stab_W(gD)=Stab_W(D).; The converse stated in the NB does not follow merely from commutation; it was read but not independently proved. Freeness, existence, and uniqueness assertions were likewise not verified.
